---README---
# SlopArena

**An open-source 3D platform fighter built around expressive movement, knockback, and compact hero-style kits.**

SlopArena takes the platform-fighter fundamentals of movement, damage percent, recovery, edge pressure, and launching opponents off the stage, then gives each fighter a small set of distinctive specials and tools to play around.

The goal is a game that is readable and competitive without taking itself too seriously: strong character identities, generous 3D hitboxes, expressive movement, and plenty of room for stupid things to happen.

> **Current state:** SlopArena is preparing a playable friends demo with four admitted cooked demo-roster packages: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. Package admission does not prove kit completeness or player acceptance. Character execution is cooked-only; Nilus and the old LMB combo compatibility path were retired on 2026-10-02. See the [playable friends demo reset](docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md) for current product work.

## The game

SlopArena combines:

- camera-relative 8-direction movement, jump arcs, double jumps, fast-fall, ledges, and Dash;
- Smash-style damage percent, Knockback, Hitstun, Hitstop, Combo Influence, Clash, and Burst;
- readable hero kits with generous 3D hitboxes and meaningful recovery, zoning, and finisher choices;
- a server-authoritative GameServer for online matches and a local Shared simulation for prediction and training.

Each kit has a canonical **16-entry grid**: grounded and aerial variants for normals `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` and specials `A`, `E`, `R`, `F`. `LMB` and `RMB` are not persisted move identities; physical controls map to the canonical slots through the client input layer.

Solo uses an attacking CPU at the selected difficulty. Training starts with one idle CPU and keeps its controls visible on the HUD. Press Escape or controller Start to adjust Idle, Attack, Shield, or Avoid behavior, difficulty, and damage, or reset damage and positions. Turn off “Show during play” to hide the panel during gameplay; it always appears while paused.

### Gamepad controls

Left Stick moves; Right Stick controls the camera and ability aim. Face buttons South/East/West/North use normals 1/2/3/4; hold LB with those buttons for specials A/E/R/F. The selected move stays fixed until its face button is released. RB jumps, LT crouches/slides/fast-falls, RT dashes, D-pad Left bursts, L3 faces the camera, R3 toggles target lock, and Start pauses. Remap buttons and the special modifier under Settings → Controls → Controller.

## Current roster

| Fighter | Style | Content status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [**FightGuy**](docs/characters/fightguy.md) | Close-range martial-arts brawler with Ki Shot, Rising Dragon, Cyclone Kick, and Fist of Fury | Admitted cooked package |
| [**Manki**](docs/characters/manki.md) | Explosive all-rounder / jetpack-bazooka skirmisher with bombs and aerosol area denial | Admitted cooked package |
| [**Wibou**](docs/characters/wibou.md) | Mid-range kitsune sword-spacing duelist focused on launches and air juggles | Admitted cooked package |
| [**Bonk**](docs/characters/bonk.md) | Greatsword fighter with sword-reach normals, targeted jump-slam recovery, and Blade Storm | Admitted cooked package; avatar visual/pose review pending |

Package admission identifies content accepted by the cooked roster manifest; it does not by itself establish kit completeness or player acceptance.

## Development

The game is built in **Unity 6** with a pure C# simulation shared by the client and GameServer. The simulation advances at **60 Hz**, keeps gameplay deterministic, and supports client prediction with server reconciliation and rollback.

### Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SlopArena.git
cd SlopArena
```

Install .NET SDK 8 to work on the simulation, server, or C# tools. A clean clone
supports these checks without Unity or the local art installation:

```bash
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
```

The root solution also supports ordinary C# IDE navigation. See the
[tool inventory](tools/README.md) for the maintained command-line tools.

The Unity client requires Unity `6000.0.78f1`, the separately installed
Animancer package, and exact local rig/animation/presentation assets. A stock
clone cannot compile and play the complete client. Follow the
[Unity setup instructions](CONTRIBUTING.md#unity-client-and-authoring) before
opening the project; Shared must be built for Unity after those prerequisites
are available.

Run the development GameServer from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet run --project src/Server/ -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- src/Server/server.json
```

Its development configuration expects a local Master server for registration.
See the [local stack](deploy/local/README.md) for the separate Master checkout
and integration setup.

Explore the [knockback visual comparison](tools/KnockbackVisuals/README.md) to watch saved before/after trajectories for all four fighters. Run `python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py` and open http://localhost:8765/, or open the standalone HTML directly in a browser.

## Architecture in one view

```text
Unity client ── input ──► Shared ServerSimulation ◄── input/state ── GameServer
     │                            │
     └── render authoritative state/events

Editable Character Package
  package.json + character.json + CharacterAssetCatalog.asset
                    │
                    ▼
       Shared compiler + Unity asset cook
                    │
                    ▼
Immutable content-cooked package
  manifest + runtime definition + poses + client bindings
```

The server and client consume the same cooked deterministic representation. Runtime matches pin package IDs, versions, hashes, dependencies, and capability versions in an immutable Match Content Catalog. Raw authoring JSON is cook input, not a runtime contract.

Explore the [interactive runtime architecture diagram](docs/generated/runtime-architecture.html) for component relationships, trust boundaries, and the primary runtime path.

The longer-term direction is cautious Workshop/package support: creators compose approved deterministic primitives and package-owned assets; they do not ship arbitrary simulation code, native plugins, or direct Unity-path dependencies. See [ADR-0022](docs/adr/0022-workshop-first-content-architecture.md) through [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-ability-lab-canonical-slot-projection.md).

## FightGuy and Ability Lab

FightGuy demonstrates the package-native workflow:

- edit `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/fightguy/`;
- inspect and cook through the Unity CLI;
- validate source, asset bindings, deterministic pose data, generated client bindings, and hashes;
- load the immutable result in Ability Lab, Training, PvP, and GameServer paths.

```bash
unity command --project-path client/Unity \
  sloparena.character.inspect --target fightguy --format json
unity command --project-path client/Unity \
  sloparena.character.cook --target fightguy --format json
```

Ability Lab is the primary gameplay editor for package drafts. It previews valid drafts through the same cooked definition and interpreter used by the game; an invalid draft is never silently substituted into a match.

To add a new character, start with [Adding a Character](docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md). Do not copy the legacy C# registry path for new work.

### SlopBot creator guide

[SlopBot skills](skills/README.md) provide guided or fast project orientation and
humanoid character creation with explicit asset/tool handoffs, bounded animation
adaptation, and resumable local progress. Instructions are harness-neutral;
execution requires supported tools and approval. The next-character verified
package/local-play run remains the public-release gate.

## Documentation

Start with the [documentation map](docs/README.md), then read:

- [Architecture overview](docs/architecture-overview.md)
- [Combat systems](docs/systems/combat-systems.md)
- [Ability architecture](docs/systems/ability-architecture.md)
- [Ability Lab](docs/systems/ability-lab.md)
- [Animation system](docs/systems/animation-system.md)
- [Netcode architecture](docs/systems/netcode-architecture.md)
- [Testing and verification](docs/testing.md)
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Contributing

Issues, design feedback, code, art, documentation, and testing are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. This project uses the [MIT license](LICENSE) and follows the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

Thank you to the artists and developers behind the assets and tools used here. See [Credits](CREDITS.md) for their names and work.

## AI usage

SlopArena uses agent-assisted development and generated art as practical tools. Contributions remain reviewed project work: determinism, licensing, gameplay correctness, and maintainability matter more than how an asset or patch was produced.

Coding assistants use the same public [project instructions](AGENTS.md) and
[task workflows](skills/README.md). See [agent setup](docs/contributing/agents.md)
for Codex, OMP, Claude Code and direct-file use.

# SlopArena

SlopArena is a Unity 6 C# 3D platform fighter with a server-authoritative 60 Hz simulation. Prioritize the four-character friends demo and first remote feedback over platform expansion; follow `docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md`. Domain vocabulary lives in `CONTEXT.md`; the documentation map is `docs/README.md`.

## Policy

- Explain the problem and intended change once, then complete the approved scope. Reuse authorization already given; approval covers the bounded task, not a new confirmation for every step.
- Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and explicitly selected checkouts. Never stage every file in a shared dirty tree. Commit and push require explicit authorization: commit authorizes a commit, push authorizes pushing existing commits, and commit push authorizes both. Reading or invoking a skill grants neither. Follow `docs/contributing/conventions.md`; rewrite or squash history only when requested.
- Ask before installing tools. User-supplied numeric choices are binding; raise a correctness issue once if needed, then follow the agreed value.
- For architecture changes, document options and get approval first. State the problem and intended change before editing; trace input → catalog/package → Shared simulation → state/event → Unity presentation when debugging.

## Where things are

- `src/Shared/` owns the compiler, cooked runtime model, deterministic simulation, codecs, and rollback primitives; its `netstandard2.1` build normally copies the Shared plugin into `client/Unity/Assets/Plugins/SlopArena.Shared/`.
- `src/Server/` hosts the headless GameServer and match orchestration. The Master server is a separate repository for lobby/meta work; it does not simulate matches.
- `client/Unity/Assets/Scripts/` owns input, presentation, networking, UI, and editor tooling. `client/Unity/Assets/AbilityLab/` owns package editing and authoritative preview. Shared coverage lives in `tests/Shared.Tests/`.
- For new character work, read `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md`: edit `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/<package>/package.json` for identity/version/dependencies/license/attribution, `character.json` for gameplay and canonical slots, and `CharacterAssetCatalog.asset` for Unity bindings. `content-cooked/<package>/` is the immutable runtime result, not authoring source.
- Use `docs/architecture-overview.md` for runtime boundaries, `docs/systems/ability-architecture.md` for cooked abilities, `docs/systems/combat-systems.md` for combat, and `docs/systems/netcode-architecture.md` for prediction/rollback.
- For live canonical Unity Editor/Pipeline work, read `docs/contributing/unity-cli.md` and `docs/contributing/unity-editor-coordination.md` before operating. Use your own caller identity under that protocol; wait for your own bounded runtime lease, never request insertion into another owner's batch. Historical Markdown ownership and active panes are not authority. For verification, read `docs/testing.md`.

## Skills and setup

Maintained workflows live in [skills/](skills/README.md). `.agents/skills/` and
`.omp/skills/` are generated discovery adapters. Load only task-relevant workflows.
Read [agent setup](docs/contributing/agents.md) for discovery, checkout and tool
boundaries. No private workspace, BMAD installation or specific IDE is required.

For GitHub issue work, follow [issue tracking](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md) and
[triage labels](docs/agents/triage-labels.md). Project context is a single root
`CONTEXT.md` with `docs/adr/`; see [domain guidance](docs/agents/domain.md).

## Running and verifying

- For offline Shared/Server builds and tests use `-p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true`. Copying a plugin into an open Editor requires your own bounded gateway lease and settled imports.
- Choose the applicable mode in `docs/testing.md`: local iteration, integrated change, or distributable demo. Keep focused behavioral coverage and applicable Shared/Server/Unity/package checks; do not force a publishing cook or unrelated runtime checks for ordinary tuning.
- For Unity-facing implementation, leave a short Test in Unity checklist in the gitignored root `TESTING-UNITY.md`. Editor operations use the approved canonical project through the gateway, not a worktree-local connection or unowned raw CLI. Worktree agents share the same runtime lease and honor source windows; never silently substitute main for an invalid explicit target.

## Conventions that differ from defaults

- Keep gameplay authority in Shared/GameServer: `ServerSimulation` runs on the server and on client local/prediction tracks. Training uses `LocalSimulationBridge`; PvP uses `RollbackSimulationBridge` with `LocalTrack`, `PredictedTrack`, and `RawTrack` as appropriate. Unity `PlayerRenderer` consumes state and semantic events; Unity physics, animation callbacks, VFX, and audio never decide damage, hit results, timing, or admission.
- Keep `src/Shared/` free of Unity types and engine physics queries. Use deterministic math and existing `SpellResolver`/geometry APIs for collision. Represent gameplay durations in 60 Hz ticks, normally `ushort`; preserve server/client Shared equivalence and immutable match content.
- New characters use the package-native path. The Shared compiler and Unity cook produce normalized runtime definitions, deterministic poses, generated client bindings, and a manifest; the Match Content Catalog pins package IDs, versions, dependencies, capability versions, and hashes. Raw authoring JSON is cook input, never the runtime contract.
- Use the canonical 16-entry grid: ground and air variants of `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `A`, `E`, `R`, and `F`. Physical controls are adapters, not persisted move identity; use semantic package IDs and canonical slot projection, not a second mapping.
- Author new abilities as fixed cooked timelines with ordered typed/versioned operations. Engine-owned deterministic primitives own movement, hitboxes, projectiles, damage, Knockback, Hitstun, Hitstop, Clash, Burst, timing locks, and presentation events. `ServerAbility` remains a Shared lifecycle seam for `CookedTimelineAbility` and trusted built-in capabilities—not the universal new-content model. Nilus and legacy character/slot factory dispatch have been removed.
- Only the trusted built-in cook profile may admit FightGuy's temporary `slop.internal.*` capabilities; Workshop/package content cannot self-grant access. Each exception needs an owner and migration path.
- Use `MonoBehaviour.Update`/`FixedUpdate` and Unity InputSystem APIs. Animancer plays semantic package bindings directly; do not give AnimatorController gameplay ownership.
- Reuse existing infrastructure before adding abstractions.

## Known pitfalls

- FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk are package-native roster characters; admission does not prove kit completeness or player acceptance. Nilus, the Compatibility preview tab, and the old LMB combo classes are retired. Do not recreate a legacy character execution path.
- Warp is not a current gameplay contract. Do not add or document Warp mechanics as new behavior; use current movement, targeting, Dash, and recovery rules in `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/systems/combat-systems.md`.


## Current release and operations routing

Routine Steam/VPS releases follow `skills/sloparena-build-export/SKILL.md`
and `docs/systems/release-pipeline.md`: isolated licensed Unity client build,
coordinated GitHub Actions deployment, then manual Steam default activation.
The build does not operate the canonical Editor or require its lease/shutdown.
Use `skills/sloparena-ops/SKILL.md` for read-only match diagnostics and the
two exact permitted VPS log commands. Reuse approvals/access already given
within scope; do not repeat unrelated historical verification or require a
privileged status session before reading logs.
=====CONTRIBUTING=====
# Contributing to SlopArena

SlopArena welcomes code, gameplay design, art, documentation, and playtesting contributions. All project communication and code use English. Read the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.

## Development setup

Clone the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SlopArena.git
cd SlopArena
```

The repository has three runtime layers:

- `src/Shared/` — pure C# `netstandard2.1` deterministic simulation and content compiler;
- `src/Server/` — headless .NET GameServer and match orchestration;
- `client/Unity/` — Unity presentation, input, networking, Ability Lab, and asset cooking.

### Simulation, server, and command-line tools

Install .NET SDK 8 through [dotnet.microsoft.com](https://dotnet.microsoft.com).
The root solution includes Shared, Server, their tests, and the maintained
[C# tools](tools/README.md). Build and test from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
```

These paths work without Unity or the ignored local art. The property prevents
offline .NET checks from copying plugins into an open Unity Editor. You can also
build/test a single affected project. Documentation checks require Python 3;
the optional agent-tool tests require Node 22.18 or newer. Exact commands live
in [quality checks](docs/contributing/quality.md).

### Unity client and authoring

The complete Unity client currently needs a local asset installation. Before
opening it, provide:

- Unity `6000.0.78f1` through [Unity Hub](https://unity.com/download);
- the required Animancer package under `client/Unity/Packages/com.kybernetik.animancer/`
  (the recorded maintainer installation is 8.4.0);
- the exact rigs, clips, VFX, audio and stage presentation assets referenced by
  the character catalogs and scenes, preserving their Unity metadata and import
  settings.

Animancer and restricted/local art are excluded from Git. A general download
of similarly named packs does not establish the required bindings. Consult
[asset source and license notes](docs/assets/credits-and-licenses.md) and
[asset conventions](docs/contributing/conventions.md); supply only assets you
are entitled to use. The worktree package-link script reuses an existing local
installation and does not provision a fresh contributor checkout.

The [Unity setup guide](docs/contributing/unity-setup.md) records dependency
ownership, exact input requirements, and the read-only
`python3 tools/check_unity_setup.py` preflight. Run it after provisioning the
Shared plugin and local assets; its result does not replace Unity compilation.

For initial setup with this Unity project closed, generate its Shared DLL:

```bash
dotnet build src/Shared/ --nologo
```

This intentional build copies only the Shared DLL and its PDB into
`client/Unity/Assets/Plugins/SlopArena.Shared/`. If the canonical Editor is
already open, follow the [Editor coordination protocol](docs/contributing/unity-editor-coordination.md)
and acquire your own bounded gateway hold before that copy. Then open
`client/Unity/` in Unity Hub, open the tracked `Frontend` scene, and inspect
compilation errors before using Training or Ability Lab. Follow
[Unity CLI](docs/contributing/unity-cli.md) and [testing](docs/testing.md) for
the affected workflow.

## Agent tooling

Project instructions live in root [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md); maintained workflows live
in [skills/](skills/README.md). Codex and OMP have generated discovery adapters;
Claude Code and other file-capable assistants can read the same public sources.
See [agent setup](docs/contributing/agents.md) for discovery, selected checkouts,
manual handoffs and explicit invocation policy. No private workspace or BMAD
installation is required.

The public [root solution](SlopArena.sln) includes Shared, Server, their tests
and C# tools. `.omp/lsp.json` invokes `omnisharp` on PATH with this solution when
OMP starts at the game root. Configure your own installed
language server if needed; this does not install it or generate Unity metadata.
Unity semantic navigation uses Editor-generated projects and the same bounded
lease protocol as other live Editor work. Compilation/presentation checks use
[Unity CLI](docs/contributing/unity-cli.md).

Routine numerical tuning does not automatically require new goldens. Prefer
focused behavioral assertions for mechanics; use the
[kit regression workflow](skills/sloparena-kit-regression-testing/SKILL.md) for
explicit scenario coverage and deliberate golden maintenance.

## Core rules

- The Shared simulation is the gameplay authority. Do not implement gameplay mechanics only in Unity.
- Keep `src/Shared/` free of Unity types and physics queries. Use the existing deterministic math and resolver APIs.
- Represent gameplay time in 60 Hz simulation ticks. Do not replace tick durations with frame-rate-dependent seconds.
- The client renders authoritative state and presentation events. Visuals, animation, VFX, and audio must not feed back into simulation.
- Preserve immutable package and match-content identity. A failed or stale cook must not silently fall back to another definition.
- Keep changes focused. Follow the repository's existing C# and Unity conventions instead of introducing parallel abstractions.

## Character contributions

New characters use the package-native workflow. Start with [Adding a Character](docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md). The editable package lives under `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/<package>/` and contains:

The current product target is a playable friends demo with Manki, FightGuy, Wibou, and
Bonk. Package authoring remains technically supported, but a fifth character is not a demo
prerequisite. Nilus compatibility has been removed; characters use cooked packages only.

- `package.json` for package identity, dependencies, creator, license, and attribution;
- `character.json` for gameplay semantics and the canonical 16-slot move grid;
- `CharacterAssetCatalog.asset` for package-local Unity asset bindings.

Cooked runtime content belongs under `content-cooked/<package>/` and is admitted through the cooked roster manifest. Do not add a registry factory, raw runtime JSON loader, manual FightGuy animation configuration, or standalone skeleton payload for new work. There is no legacy character execution fallback.

## Verification

Choose the applicable mode in [Testing and verification](docs/testing.md):

- **Local iteration:** use the Editor development catalog and affected Ability Lab or
  Training path; do not publish a package for every tuning edit.
- **Integrated change:** run focused behavioral coverage and the applicable Shared,
  Server, Unity, or package checks.
- **Distributable demo:** cook accepted content, verify roster-complete publish outputs,
  build the client/server, and exercise the packaged join-to-rematch path.

Use [Unity CLI](docs/contributing/unity-cli.md) for concrete commands. Preserve the
Shared/server authority, exact package identity, and fail-closed cook behavior.

## Pull requests

1. Create a focused branch.
2. Explain the user-visible behavior and the authoritative data path.
3. Include the verification commands and their results.
4. Link relevant issues, ADRs, or design documents.
5. Keep generated artifacts and unrelated local changes out of the pull request.

Do not commit or push on behalf of another contributor. Follow the repository's [commit conventions](docs/contributing/conventions.md) when creating commits.

## Non-code contributions

Open an issue or pull request for:

- fighter and move design;
- 3D models, animation, VFX, audio, or arena work;
- UI and accessibility improvements;
- documentation and research;
- reproducible playtest findings.

For design changes, describe the intended counterplay, timing, and interaction with the shared simulation before implementation.

of the public project workflows.

=====PRODUCT=====
# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

adaptive

## Users

Primary users are friends playing SlopArena online. They need to join a match, understand each fighter quickly, and complete short remote matches without requiring every player to operate hosting or networking infrastructure.

## Product Purpose

SlopArena is an open-source 3D platform fighter built around expressive movement, knockback, compact hero-style kits, and room for unexpected play. The immediate product goal is a playable friends demo that gets real remote feedback on four admitted cooked characters: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk.

Success means friends can enter a match, understand what happened, and have enough readable, expressive interaction to want another round. Package admission is not treated as proof of kit completeness or player acceptance.

## Positioning

SlopArena's distinctive mechanism is a server-authoritative 60 Hz simulation shared by the Unity client and GameServer. The same deterministic gameplay model supports training, prediction, reconciliation, rollback, and online matches while leaving presentation in the client.

The combat identity combines camera-relative 8-direction movement, jump arcs, double jumps, fast-fall, ledges, Dash, damage percent, Knockback, Hitstun, Hitstop, Combo Influence, Clash, Burst, and compact fighter kits with meaningful recovery, zoning, and finisher choices.

## Operating Context

The primary operating context is Unity 6 on desktop, with a local training flow and online matches through a GameServer. A master server manages browser, lobby, character-select, and results flow; it does not simulate matches.

Players move through the MatchFlow: Server Browser, Lobby Room, Character Select, Countdown, Fight, Results, and Lobby Room. Non-technical players should be able to use an OfficialServer; technical players may use HostAndPlay.

Gameplay runs at 60 Hz. The client renders authoritative state and semantic presentation events; the Shared simulation remains the gameplay authority.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Each character uses a canonical 16-entry grid: grounded and aerial variants of normals `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` and specials `A`, `E`, `R`, `F`.
- Physical controls are input adapters and are not persisted move identities.
- New characters are package-native. Editable packages live under `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/<package>/` and cook into immutable runtime artifacts under `content-cooked/<package>/`.
- Match Content Catalogs pin exact package IDs, versions, dependencies, capability versions, and hashes.
- Raw authoring JSON is cook input, not the runtime contract.
- Server-side simulation is authoritative. Unity physics, animation callbacks, VFX, and audio are presentation or authoring aids only.
- Shared simulation code remains free of Unity types and engine physics queries.
- Current admitted demo roster: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. Nilus and its legacy character execution path are retired.
- The longer-term Workshop direction permits approved deterministic primitives and package-owned assets, not arbitrary simulation code, native plugins, or direct Unity-path dependencies.
- The current implementation targets Unity 6 desktop. SlopArena also has a separate web presentation surface; the Impeccable platform value `adaptive` records that the product spans these first-party surfaces rather than asserting a mobile-native target.

## Brand Commitments

The shared identity is **low-poly underground toy-fight-club, with DIY internet-game energy**: scavenged construction, chunky silhouettes, curated asset-pack collage, and cool fighting imagery with jokes second. “Toy” is a construction metaphor, not a requirement for literal plastic or cute styling. The website is the strongest existing graphic reference, not a fully approved implementation.

Target graphic primary actions and selection use Action Yellow (`#FFCC22`). Archivo Black is the target shared name-mark and display voice; marketing pairs it with Space Mono. Native short utility labels may use mono where practical, while dense settings and HUD text should remain readable sans. Paper, Ink, and orange values remain local to each surface; existing native orange `#E05C2A` and marketing orange `#F05B35` are retained.

The canonical visual-language guide is `docs/design/visual-language.md`; art conventions remain authoritative for 3D and assets. The sibling repository `../SlopArena-web` is the web graphic reference.

**Status:** SlopArena is unreleased, developed by a solo developer, and is not on Steam. The player-facing identity rollout is implemented. Frontend pages use the user's authored paper background; Home has separate mode/poster/announcement columns. Chat is an absolute user-sized overlay in menus and gameplay and does not influence underlying composition. Settings and match overlays retain readable neutral fields. The separately approved gameplay HUD now has fight-card player panels with clear lives, four paired tickets displaying all eight moves with live ground/air names and effective bindings, shared damage-tier colors, and a persistent target marker with an optional overhead percentage. 3D arenas, existing navigation, gameplay data/authority, and networking are preserved. Connected-room, distributable-player, creator/Ability Lab, website, and release-copy migration are not claimed; the website still has the misleading Steam CTA.

## Evidence on Hand

- `README.md` contains the current product description, four-character demo status, architecture, development setup, and roster summary.
- `CONTEXT.md` defines the canonical domain vocabulary and settled mechanics.
- `docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md` defines the current demo priority.
- `docs/design/visual-language.md` defines the shared presentation grammar.
- `content-cooked/` contains cooked runtime artifacts for the admitted packages.
- `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/` contains package-native authoring sources and asset catalogs.
- The repository has no confirmed testimonials, press claims, benchmark claims, or external player-acceptance evidence. Future surfaces must not fabricate them.

## Product Principles

1. Make the next player action and the last gameplay event immediately understandable.
2. Preserve deterministic, server-authoritative gameplay across local and online paths.
3. Give each fighter a compact, readable identity with meaningful counterplay.
4. Prefer honest prototype energy over generic polish or unsupported claims.
5. Expand creator content through immutable, reviewable, deterministic packages.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Gameplay and UI must not rely on color alone for status, player identity, or combat information. Preserve readable contrast, stable HUD information, clear focus and confirmation states, and reduced-motion behavior for non-gameplay presentation where the platform supports it.

name: slopbot-character
description: Plan and complete an approved SlopArena humanoid character package using the project's existing character, Ability Lab, and acceptance workflows.
---

# SlopBot Character

Use this helper for the character work owned by the selected SlopArena checkout. The entry skill `slopbot` owns approvals, interaction mode, selected checkout, and the small `.slopbot/<package-or-goal>.md` progress record. If invoked directly, first load those shared instructions from the harness skill loader or sibling `../slopbot/SKILL.md`; if unavailable, stop rather than bypassing them. Resolve every project document below from the user's selected checkout, never from this installed helper's directory or an author's workspace path. Work only within the approved character scope; a missing tool means an explicit user handoff or blocker, not a claim of action.

## Establish the agreed character and assets

Start with the user's actual goal, existing package/source, approved concept or kit, and progress record. Resume at the unresolved need; do not repeat settled design decisions. If the kit is not approved, use game-root `docs/characters/character-kit-design-principles.md` to agree a humanoid fighter's role, movement/recovery, eight normals, four specials, intended interactions, and desired presentation. Record the decisions and required asset roles before integration. Game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` owns implementation and acceptance; `docs/characters/character-import-checklist.md` is a checkpoint, not a substitute.

For every model, rig, animation clip, image, or effect, identify the actual source and exact intended asset; record provenance, creator/source URL or supplier, applicable license, attribution, and whether redistribution into repository/package is permitted. A service/library handoff requires the user to select/provide the assets and licensing evidence. Do not assume a license, generate or fetch assets, author a full model/custom rig/original motion, or silently include non-redistributable content. Preserve source files and Unity `.meta` files. If an ordinary humanoid rig, required clip, license, or supported tool is missing, state the concrete input and expected proof needed from the user; inspect the returned asset before resuming.

Map the concept onto existing gameplay primitives and the current Shared implementation, not an invented mechanic. Confirm a proposed operation/capability is supported by current project documentation/source before relying on it. If an essential interaction is unsupported, name it, pause that branch, and request a separately scoped engine task; present alternatives only as options for approval. Author the agreed package gameplay through existing primitives; do not substitute a different design or extend Shared/server engine code as part of integration.

## Integrate source and author the kit

The project has distinct owners: `package.json` for identity/version/creator/license/attribution/dependencies, `character.json` for gameplay source and presentation IDs, and `CharacterAssetCatalog.asset` for Unity rig and semantic clip bindings. Source package location and the authoring-ready template seam are documented in game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` and `docs/systems/ability-lab.md`. Do not invent a package-creation button: current docs identify `AbilityLabPackageWorkspace.NewPackage` as the creation seam but no user-facing creation flow. If no supported tool or authorized operator can invoke that seam, hand off the approved package specification and required result; do not create an ad hoc package or claim creation.

Bind real clips to exact semantic IDs on the actual imported Humanoid rig; preserve unique deterministic pose-track IDs and resolve Avatar/binding diagnostics instead of borrowing another fighter's fallback. If model cleanup or rig repair is needed, name that external/separate scope and route to game-root `docs/characters/character-model-polish.md`. Optional splash art/VFX are supplied/sourced only: verify ownership and the actual consuming surface/binding, and leave them out if not selected. Once selected as required presentation, their integration must be verified rather than silently omitted.

Resolve all sixteen canonical grounded/air slots deliberately from the agreed kit. Approved aliases and move/clip reuse count; a smaller number of independent source entries is not itself an incomplete kit. Use the compiler/inspect resolved projection and approved semantics, not counts or labels alone, to judge coverage. Starter template values are not approved moves. Keep controls/labels distinct from persisted slot identities. Use the existing Slop Editor/Ability Lab Moves workspace for live drafts, timeline, source-stage fields, SceneView overlays, supported operation inspectors, and Undo; do not guess controls or create a second mapping. Through supported Shared/Training paths, observe timing, contact/miss, hitboxes, damage, recovery, movement and selected mechanics; change the relevant draft input and retest. Shared/server owns outcomes; if a mechanic cannot be authored through existing primitives, pause at the engine-task boundary.

## Inspect, cook, admit, and play

Before cooking, resolve supported operations and Editor ownership from game-root `docs/contributing/unity-cli.md`; command examples are not permission to bypass ownership or require an author's private workspace. Discover available supported commands and use `sloparena.character.inspect` read-only on the actual package when authorized. Resolve identity, canonical-slot, source/catalog, rig, dependency, stale-input, and structured diagnostics. If the required tool/owned route is unavailable, hand off the exact package and expected inspect evidence; do not report verification.

Persistence is through the documented Ability Lab **SAVE + COOK** path (or its supported native command flow), not raw edits to generated output. A successful cook must identify the exact current package and its four fresh payloads/hashes; a failed cook is a failure even if it preserves an older valid artifact. Re-inspect after changes and ensure evidence refers to current source, rig, catalog, and dependencies. Do not edit cooked payloads or generated catalog cache as source.

After a successful current cook, complete the applicable focused compiler/catalog/package checks and kit regression evidence specified by game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` and `docs/testing.md`. Test, change, and retest behavior that failed or needed tuning; report actual observations and limitations. Add or refresh exact roster admission only through the documented workflow and after required checks/presentation are valid. Verify package identity/version/hashes/dependencies and the exact local roster requirement against fresh content; source-only discovery or a transient draft does not count.

Open the accepted cooked package in Ability Lab to check identity, slot projection, semantic bindings, preview, and diagnostics; exercise Training and applicable local gameplay with that same persisted package. Confirm the roster selects it and the complete agreed kit is actually exercised using admitted content, not an in-memory draft, stale cook, or prior fighter. Record observed checks, input identities/hashes, outcome, and blockers. No online play, publication, or broader release claim follows from local acceptance.

## Resume and handoff

On resume, compare recorded approvals, kit, asset provenance, source/package identity, bindings, cook hashes, roster requirement, and test/play evidence with current files and diagnostics. Invalidate only checks whose inputs changed. Preserve valid prior work. A useful handoff names the exact missing asset/tool/permission, the owner or supported documented route when known, the expected output/evidence, and the next step after it is supplied; never turn instructions into claimed completion.

    r"python3?\s+(?P<python>[^-\s\\][^\s\\]*)|bun\s+(?P<bun>[^-\s\\][^\s\\]*))"
)
QUALITY_REFERENCED_PATH = re.compile(r"`(?P<path>(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/)*[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)`")


def check_quality_commands(errors: list[str], files: list[Path]) -> None:
    source = Path("docs/contributing/quality.md")
    if source not in files:
        return
    text = (ROOT / source).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    for match in QUALITY_REFERENCED_PATH.finditer(text):
        target = match.group("path")
        if "/" not in target and not target.endswith((".csproj", ".sln")):
            continue
        if not (ROOT / target).is_file():
            line = text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1
            errors.append(f"{source}:{line}: missing referenced workflow/script/project {target}")
    for block in QUALITY_CODE_BLOCK.finditer(text):
        for match in QUALITY_COMMAND.finditer(block.group(1)):
            make_target = match.group("make")
            unittest_start = match.group("unittest_start")
            unittest_pattern = match.group("unittest_pattern")
            target = make_target or match.group("dotnet") or match.group("python") or match.group("bun") or unittest_start
            if make_target:
                makefile = ROOT / "Makefile"
                targets: set[str] = set()
                if makefile.is_file():
                    for line in makefile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
                        if line and not line[0].isspace() and ":" in line:
                            targets.update(line.split(":", 1)[0].split())
                exists = make_target in targets
            elif unittest_start:
                test_dir = ROOT / unittest_start
                exists = test_dir.is_dir() and any(path.is_file() for path in test_dir.glob(unittest_pattern))
            elif match.group("python") or match.group("bun") or target.endswith((".csproj", ".sln")):
                exists = (ROOT / target).is_file()
            else:
                exists = (ROOT / target).is_dir()
            if not exists:
                line = text.count("\n", 0, block.start(1) + match.start()) + 1
                errors.append(f"{source}:{line}: missing executable target/path {target}")

  ## 2. Stage creation
  
  **(a) What it is:** Design an arena with an AI helper. You talk through the layout, block it out in grey boxes, then bake real collision, add art, and test it in Training.
  
  **(b) Entry point:**

  **(e) Type:** AI-driven skills. The human playtest is a manual step, and the Blender generators can be run by hand.
  
  ## 3. Animation test / animation work
  
  **(a) What it is:** Make or fix a fighter's attack animation and preview it on the real character before it goes in.

The tracked scenes are AbilityLab, Arcade_*, Arena_Offline/PvP, Frontend, Prototypes/*, VisualBaselineCapture and hub.

  **(e) Type:** AI-driven.
  
  ## 4. Ability Lab (branded "Slop Editor" in its UI)
  
  **(a) What it is:** A Unity editor window where you pick a fighter, scrub each attack frame by frame, see hitboxes and hurtboxes, drag timings, and test hits against a dummy.
  
  **(b) Entry point:** `Tools → SlopArena → Ability Lab` (on origin: `Tools → SLOPArena → Ability Lab`). Agents can also drive it through `sloparena.lab.open|run|preview|inspect|capture`.
  
  **(c) Prerequisites:** Full Unity plus private art. Authoritative preview needs the cooked package and rig. No AI needed.
  
  **(d) What a human can do:**
  - Move through the timeline: Play, ±1 frame, scrub, 0.5×–4× zoom.
  - Toggle Hitboxes, Hurtboxes and Motion overlays.
  - Drag timeline markers and hitbox bodies, resize hitbox endpoints, and use the SceneView hitbox radius handle.
  - Add a forward lunge, targeted leap or charged dash, and edit projectile fields.
  - Edit VFX cues (tick, bone, transform) and assign presentation assets.
  - Edit grab capture geometry, and (on origin) startup aim correction.
  - Run Scenario Controls against an idle or shielding opponent at a chosen distance, damage, facing and charge, and see hit, block, miss or grab outcomes.
  - Use Undo/Redo, detach the fields pane, and **Save + Cook**.
  
  **Maturity: proven and in daily use.** 27 commits since `0062992d` (2026-08-23), the latest being `45784791` (2026-10-16: its own private preview scene, so it no longer needs the AbilityLab scene). It has a self-test suite under `Tools/…/Tests/Ability Lab *`. **No screenshots are tracked anywhere in `docs/`.** Captures go to the gitignored `.ability-lab-cache/`.
  
  **(e) Type:** Human UI, also agent-drivable.
  
  ## 5. Training mode (and Solo Arcade on origin)
  
  **(a) What it is:** Practice against a CPU you can set to stand still, attack, shield or run away, with adjustable difficulty and damage.
  
  **(b) Entry point:**

  **(c) Prerequisites:** A Windows build from the maintainer (zip or Steam Playtest; see `PLAY_GUIDE.md` and `release-playtest.yml`) or the full Unity setup. No AI.
  
  **(d) Maturity: proven, shipped in playtest builds.**
  - `CpuBehavior` and `CpuDifficulty` live in `src/Shared/AI/HeuristicBotPolicy.cs` and `BotDifficultyProfile.cs`.

  - **Solo Arcade (origin only):**
    - Slopball supports all four fighters and keeps local personal bests; FightGuy also has the Sanctuary course. Both are reachable from an offline menu.
    - `docs/design/arcade.md`: "Phases 1–4 are implemented… Full-course polish and human acceptance remain ahead."
  - Origin also has a 4-CPU filming preview (`aaeb041f`, `docs/testing/cpu-showcase.md`). It is an Editor-only capture tool that agents run.
  
  **(e) Type:** Human (in-game).
  
  ## 6. Character model polish in Blender
  
  **(a) What it is:** Have an AI assistant clean up a 3D character (shading, holes, skin weights) inside your running Blender, with before/after comparisons.

  - Commits: `7aa594f2`, `e5886610`, `9898c097`, `f5bc2966`.

  **(e) Type:** AI-driven.
  
  ## 7. Move data and balance tooling
  
  **(a) What it is:** Command-line reports that run the real game simulation, without Unity, to print frame data, knockback paths, movement stats and bot-vs-bot match stats.
  
  **(b) Entry point:**
  - `scripts/move-data.sh` → `tools/MoveDataReport`
  - `scripts/movement-report.sh`
  - `scripts/selfplay.sh` → `SelfPlayReport`
  - `scripts/ab-diff.sh` → `AbDiffReport`

  **(c) Prerequisites:** Just the .NET 8 SDK; the tools read the tracked `content-cooked/`. The knockback viewer only needs a browser. No Unity, no AI.
  
  **(d) Maturity: proven.**
  - CI builds every tool in `SlopArena.sln` but doesn't run them.
  - Committed outputs: `fightguy-move-data.md` (08-29), fightguy selfplay and abdiff (08-18/19), wibou move-data, selfplay and abdiff (10-01), `movement.md/html` (10-16), and the knockback visuals (10-11).

  **(e) Type:** Human CLI.

  **(a) What it is:** Ideas for new modes (capture zones, volleyball, crown, moving platforms) that are written down but not built.

  ## 9. Replays
  
  **(a) What it is:** Saving and rewatching online matches. It has been designed but not built.
  
  **(b) Documents:**

  **(d) Maturity: spec only.** There are no Replay classes in `src/` or the client runtime. **Don't confuse it with** origin's `sloparena.replay.*` commands, `scripts/sloparena-replay.ts` and `docs/testing/course-replay.md`. Those replay scripted inputs against Arcade courses as a test tool.

# SLOPArena

**An open-source 3D platform fighter built around expressive movement, knockback, and compact hero-style kits.**

SLOPArena takes the platform-fighter fundamentals of movement, damage percent, recovery, edge pressure, and launching opponents off the stage, then gives each fighter a small set of distinctive specials and tools to play around.

The root [SlopArena.sln](../SlopArena.sln) is the maintained .NET build set:

To run one tool without copying the Shared plugin into Unity:

```bash

```

Use each tool's argument parser or documented usage before running it. Supply an
ignored output directory for reports. Baking tools write content and need a
deliberately selected destination; build success does not authorize overwriting
current arena data. A tool's successful run is diagnostic evidence, not acceptance

# Knockback visual comparison

Watch before/after knockback paths from the real Shared simulation, with synchronized playback, a time scrubber, and selectors for all four characters, individual normal hits, and damage percents. Orange is before; teal is after. Ordinary views use equal horizontal and vertical distance scale. The weak-pop close-up magnifies height five times and labels that magnification.

## Open the saved viewer

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py
```

Open **http://localhost:8765/**. It opens the latest saved comparison; page links switch between the original flight update and the outlier/special tuning. Use `--view original` or `--view outliers` to choose explicitly. Stop the server with Ctrl+C; use `--port 8766` if the default port is busy. The launcher resolves the viewer location from its own file, so it also works from another working directory.

You can also open [the standalone HTML](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/index.html) directly in a browser. It embeds every trajectory and requires no server, internet, Unity, or JavaScript packages. The [overview](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/overview.png), [animation](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/before-after.mp4), and [measurement report](../../docs/generated/knockback-flight-comparison.md) accompany the interactive viewer.

## Saved comparison

`comparison.json` preserves both sides of the **2026-10-11 flight-physics comparison**, including the baseline simulation hash, recording conditions, and trajectory point columns. It is a historical snapshot; editing the simulation does not silently change either side. It contains all four characters at 0%, 60%, 120%, and 200% damage before the hit, including isolated entries for multihit normals. Positions are rounded to five decimal places for visualization.

Both datasets use the same cooked move definitions. Victims are passive, with no DI, SDI, player movement, or follow-up hits; hitstop is excluded. Downward sends start above the floor. Ground contact can occur while hitstun continues, and positions stop at the end of the original report rather than extrapolating later ground carry. See the measurement report for the full method and verification.

The viewer, snapshot, template, generator, PNG, and MP4 live in normal repository paths, outside ignored artifact directories.

`outliers-comparison.json` preserves the subsequent authoring pass under the new flight model. Its [viewer](../../docs/generated/knockback-outlier-visuals/index.html) includes all normal and special hit components, projectile/explosion sends, fixed hitstun, and Dash Slash charge tiers. Components are isolated; they are not a complete special sequence. Its [report](../../docs/generated/knockback-outlier-tuning.md) records the changes and actual-contact verification.

```bash

  --comparison tools/KnockbackVisuals/outliers-comparison.json \
  --output docs/generated/knockback-outlier-visuals
```

## Development

The game is built in **Unity 6** with a pure C# simulation shared by the client and GameServer. The simulation advances at **60 Hz**, keeps gameplay deterministic, and supports client prediction with server reconciliation and rollback.

### Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SlopArena.git
cd SlopArena
```

Install .NET SDK 8 to work on the simulation, server, or C# tools. A clean clone
supports these checks without Unity or the local art installation:

```bash
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
```

The root solution also supports ordinary C# IDE navigation. See the
[tool inventory](tools/README.md) for the maintained command-line tools.

The Unity client requires Unity `6000.0.78f1`, the separately installed
Animancer package, and exact local rig/animation/presentation assets. A stock
clone cannot compile and play the complete client. Follow the
[Unity setup instructions](CONTRIBUTING.md#unity-client-and-authoring) before
opening the project; Shared must be built for Unity after those prerequisites
are available.

Run the development GameServer from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet run --project src/Server/ -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- src/Server/server.json
```

Its development configuration expects a local Master server for registration.
See the [local stack](deploy/local/README.md) for the separate Master checkout
and integration setup.

Explore the [knockback visual comparison](tools/KnockbackVisuals/README.md) to watch saved before/after trajectories for all four fighters. Run `python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py` and open http://localhost:8765/, or open the standalone HTML directly in a browser.

## Architecture in one view

```text
Unity client ── input ──► Shared ServerSimulation ◄── input/state ── GameServer
     │                            │
     └── render authoritative state/events

Editable Character Package
  package.json + character.json + CharacterAssetCatalog.asset
                    │
                    ▼
       Shared compiler + Unity asset cook
                    │
                    ▼
Immutable content-cooked package
  manifest + runtime definition + poses + client bindings
```

The server and client consume the same cooked deterministic representation. Runtime matches pin package IDs, versions, hashes, dependencies, and capability versions in an immutable Match Content Catalog. Raw authoring JSON is cook input, not a runtime contract.

Explore the [interactive runtime architecture diagram](docs/generated/runtime-architecture.html) for component relationships, trust boundaries, and the primary runtime path.

The longer-term direction is cautious Workshop/package support: creators compose approved deterministic primitives and package-owned assets; they do not ship arbitrary simulation code, native plugins, or direct Unity-path dependencies. See [ADR-0022](docs/adr/0022-workshop-first-content-architecture.md) through [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-ability-lab-canonical-slot-projection.md).

# SLOPArena **A free, open-source 3D platform fighter: rack up damage, then launch your friends off the stage.** ## Hi! > **TODO (Binoui):** your intro goes here, in your own words. ## What is SLOPArena? It's a platform fighter in the Smash family, in full 3D. Every hit adds damage, and the more damage you carry, the farther you fly, until somebody goes off the stage. Each fighter has a compact kit: eight normal attacks (four on the ground, four in the air) and four specials.

- **Four fighters:** FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. - **Six stages** to pick from, including the three above. - **Training** against a CPU you can tune, and offline **Arcade** challenges. - **Online matches** on a dedicated server, with rollback netcode. - Built in **Unity 6**. SLOPArena

A free, open-source 3D platform fighter: rack up damage, then launch your friends off the stage.

Discord · Play it · Try it in five minutes · Make stuff · Docs

Hi!

TODO (Binoui): your intro goes here, in your own words.

What is SLOPArena?

It's a platform fighter in the Smash family, in full 3D. Every hit adds damage, and the more damage you carry, the farther you fly, until somebody goes off the stage. Each fighter has a compact kit: eight normal attacks (four on the ground, four in the air) and four specials.

  • Four fighters: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk.
  • Six stages to pick from, including the three above.
  • Training against a CPU you can tune, and offline Arcade challenges.
  • Online matches on a dedicated server, with rollback netcode.
  • Built in Unity 6. The gameplay itself is a deterministic C# simulation that the game and the server share.
  • MIT licensed. Made by one developer and a lot of AI help (how AI is used).

Where it's at (October 2026): early. We're building toward a playable demo for friends. The fighters are still being tuned, no stage has had a proper group playtest yet, and making online matches reliable is the current focus. Expect rough edges, and please tell us about them.

The fighters

Fighter Style
FightGuy Close-range martial artist: Ki Shot, Rising Dragon, Cyclone Kick, and Fist of Fury
Manki Pyromaniac inventor monkey with a jetpack, a bazooka, bombs, and aerosol traps
Wibou Kitsune swordswoman who controls space with her blade, then juggles you in the air
Bonk Greatsword bruiser with long reach, a jump-slam recovery, and Blade Storm

Things you can do here

Play it

SLOPArena runs on Windows 10 and 11. The easiest way in is the Steam Playtest: ask Binoui for access on Discord. Test builds are also attached to the Releases page.

Training and Arcade work offline. Online matches need our server to be up, and they're what we're fixing right now, so they may not connect yet. The controls are below.

Try it in five minutes, no Unity needed

Install Git and the .NET 8 SDK, then:

git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SLOPArena.git
cd SLOPArena

# Watch two CPU fighters brawl in your terminal (Ctrl+C to quit)
dotnet run --project tools/SpectateView -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- --char manki

# Build everything and run the test suite
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true

That's the real game simulation running with no graphics attached. -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true keeps these commands from touching the Unity project. More things that work straight from a clone:

  • Knockback viewer: run python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py and open http://localhost:8765/ to scrub through real launch trajectories for every fighter (details).
  • HUD preview: run python3 -m http.server 8000 from the repository root and open http://localhost:8000/tools/hud-preview/ to edit the in-game HUD stylesheet and see the result live. A few icons are missing from a clean clone.
  • Reports: frame data, movement stats, and bot-vs-bot match stats from the command line. See the tool inventory.

Make stuff

These need the full Unity project, which isn't self-serve yet (see Getting set up). They're where most of the fun is, and some of them start with no setup at all.

Make your own fighter. SlopBot is an AI guide that takes you from an idea to a playable fighter: kit design, model and animation handoffs, wiring up the moves, and testing them in Training. The design part needs no Unity, so you can start today. SlopBot is brand new and nobody has finished a fighter with it yet, so you'd be the first. See Working with an AI assistant to start it, and the kit design principles for what makes a good fighter.

Design a stage. Pitch an idea, block it out in grey boxes with an AI helper, then bake the collision, dress it with art, and test it in Training. Most of the current stages went through this workflow, and stage art can also be generated in Blender with scripts. Start with the stage concepts and the stage design workflow.

Test and tune moves and animations. Ability Lab is the in-Unity editor for fighters: scrub any attack frame by frame, see and drag hitboxes, change timings, and try hits against an idle or shielding dummy. It's also where new animations get checked on the real character. See the Ability Lab guide and the animation workflow.

Fix up a 3D model. An AI assistant connected to Blender can clean up shading, holes, and skin weights on a rigged character, with before-and-after comparisons. See the model polish guide.

Everything else

Ideas, fighter designs on paper, art, VFX, sound, UI, docs, and "this felt bad when I played it" are all welcome. Open an issue (bug report or idea) or come say hi on Discord. New multiplayer modes such as capture zones, volleyball, and crown are still just ideas, so come argue about them.

# Ship PR

Take a branch that has real, tested work on it and get it in front of a human as a mergeable pull request — commit it properly, tidy the history only where tidying actually helps, push it, open or update the PR with a body a reviewer can act on, keep an eye on CI and fix what's actually broken, then hand the link back.

This is the same flow whether the working directory is a normal clone or a git worktree: git and `gh` operate on whatever is checked out in the current directory, so nothing here needs to detect or branch on worktree-ness. The only worktree-specific fact worth knowing is that the same branch can't be checked out in two worktrees at once — if a push or checkout complains about that, it means the branch is live somewhere else, not that something is broken.

## 1. Take stock before doing anything

Run `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` (see step 3 for finding `<base>`) to see what's actually here:

- Uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, both, or neither? If there's truly nothing to ship, say so instead of inventing an empty commit or PR.
- Is the current branch itself the default branch? A PR from `main` into `main` doesn't mean anything — create a new branch first, named after the work (check recent commit subjects or the diff for a topic), and continue from there.
- Untracked files: don't sweep everything into the commit with a blind `git add -A` if `git status` shows files that obviously don't belong to this task (stray scratch files, unrelated local config). Stage what belongs to the work; ask if it's genuinely ambiguous.

## 2. Commit

Look at `git log --oneline -20` first so the message matches how this repo actually writes commits — some repos use Conventional Commits (`feat(scope): …`), some don't; match what's there rather than imposing a style. Write a message that explains *why*, not just *what changed*, the same way you'd want to read it in six months.

If the session already produced one or more commits on this branch earlier, you don't need to redo this — move on to the squash decision.

## 3. Decide whether to squash — this is a judgment call, not a rule

Find the base: `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name`, or `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed 's@^refs/remotes/origin/@@'` if `gh` isn't available, falling back to `main` only if both fail. Then look at `git log --oneline origin/<base>..HEAD`.

Squashing helps when the history is noise a reviewer would have to mentally filter out: "wip", "fix typo", "address review comment", "oops", commits that revert or duplicate each other. Squashing hurts when each commit is already a coherent, well-scoped unit — a maintainer reading `git log` later benefits from seeing "add the schema field" as a separate commit from "add the migration" even though both are one PR. If the branch already has exactly one commit, there's nothing to decide.

To squash: `git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<base>)` then commit once with a message that synthesizes what the dropped commits were actually doing (not a concatenation of their subject lines). If the branch was already pushed under the old history, the next push needs `--force-with-lease`, never a bare `--force` — that still protects against clobbering something someone else pushed in the meantime.

## 4. Push

`git push -u origin <branch>` the first time (sets the upstream so `gh` and future pushes don't need `-u` again), or `git push` / `git push --force-with-lease` after that depending on whether step 3 rewrote history.

## 5. Open or update the PR

Check for an existing PR on this branch first — `gh pr view --json url,number` (exits non-zero if there isn't one) — so you never open a second PR for the same branch. If one exists, a plain push already updated its commits; only touch `gh pr edit` if the title/body genuinely need to change too.

If there's no existing PR, create one with `gh pr create --base <base> --head <branch> --title "…" --body-file <path>`. If `gh` isn't installed or `gh auth status` shows it's not logged in, fall back to the GitHub MCP tool's create-pull-request call with the same base/head/title/body.

**Share the link immediately.** The moment `gh pr create` (or `gh pr edit`) returns a URL, put it in front of the user in that same turn — don't hold it back until step 7's final report. CI watching and fix loops in step 6 can take minutes; the human wants the link the moment it exists. Step 7 is a closing status update, not the first appearance of the link.

**Body safety.** A body containing backticks, code fences, or `$(...)` is exactly the "complex quoting" case the bash tool itself warns to avoid — piping it through an inline shell heredoc risks the shell reinterpreting backticks as command substitution and silently mangling the text. Write the body to a file first (the `write` tool, e.g. `/tmp/pr-body.md`) and pass `--body-file <path>`, never an inline `--body "…"` for anything beyond a one-liner. After creating or editing, confirm with `gh pr view --json body -q .body` that what landed matches what you wrote — don't assume the first attempt took.

**Body**: check for `.github/pull_request_template.md` first and fill that in if it exists — that's the repo telling you what it wants. Otherwise use a structure like:

```markdown
Closes #<N>          <!-- only if this work traces to an issue; don't invent one -->

## Problem / motivation
<why this exists — pull from the issue or the conversation, don't restate the diff>

## Change
<what changed, grouped by area, as a short bullet list>

## Tests / verification
<what you actually ran and what it showed — reuse whatever you already verified while doing the work, don't re-verify just for the PR>
```

An issue number, if there is one, usually already surfaced earlier — in the branch name, in a commit message, or in what the user told you. Use that; don't guess a number.

## 6. Watch CI, and fix what's actually broken

Skip this whole step gracefully if the repo has no CI configured — `gh pr checks` will say so plainly, and that's not a problem to solve.

If checks are configured, `gh pr checks --watch` blocks until they conclude. On failure:

1. Pull the actual failure with `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed` (get `<run-id>` from `gh run list --branch <branch> --limit 1` or the checks output) — read the real error, don't guess from the check name.
2. Fix the root cause in the code. The same rule applies here as anywhere else: don't skip the failing test, silence the lint rule, or add a special case to make the check pass without fixing what it's actually catching.
3. Commit the fix — amend into the last commit and `push --force-with-lease` if the branch is already a single clean commit (keeps the history from step 3 clean), otherwise add a small dedicated commit, whichever keeps the same history quality you already chose in step 3.
4. Re-run `gh pr checks --watch`.

Cap this at 3 fix attempts. If it's still red after that, stop — don't keep guessing. Report exactly which check is failing, a link to the run, and what you tried each time, and hand it back.

## 7. Report back

Close the loop with a short summary: what got committed (and whether/why it got squashed), and CI status — green, "no checks configured", or still red with the specific blocker if step 6 hit its cap. Re-include the PR link here too even though it already went out in step 5 — a reviewer skimming just the final message shouldn't have to scroll up for it.

input.description: Audit Animancer dependency surface
input.prompt:
Context: SLOPArena is a Unity 6 platform fighter (public GitHub repo). Gameplay is a deterministic C# simulation in `src/Shared/`; Unity only presents it. The maintainer wants a fresh `git clone` to open, compile and run the Unity project WITHOUT the third-party Animancer package (Kybernetik), because neither Animancer Pro nor the free Lite edition may be redistributed in a public repo. I need a precise audit of how deep the Animancer dependency goes, to decide between (a) making Animancer optional behind a compile-time seam with a fallback, and (b) replacing it with an in-house player built on Unity's built-in Playables API. Read-only; thoroughness: very thorough.

Use the clean checkout at `/home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena/.worktrees/friends-onboarding` (tracked files only, matches origin/main) for everything that's tracked. The locally installed, untracked Animancer package lives ONLY in the maintainer's main checkout at `/home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena/client/Unity/Packages/com.kybernetik.animancer/` — use it only to look up assembly names and script GUIDs (its `.meta` files).

Report, with file paths and line numbers:

1. **Every tracked C# file that references Animancer** (`using Animancer`, `Animancer.` qualified names, `#if ANIMANCER`-style symbols). Group by assembly (find each file's owning `.asmdef`). List which `.asmdef` files reference the Animancer assembly (by name or GUID reference — get Animancer's asmdef name/GUID from the local package). Note `Packages/manifest.json` / `packages-lock.json` entries for it.
2. **The exact API surface used.** Every Animancer type and member touched (e.g. `AnimancerComponent`, `AnimancerState`, `AnimancerLayer`, `ClipTransition`, mixers, `AnimancerEvent`, `Play`/`TryPlay`/fade durations/`FadeMode`, `Time`/`NormalizedTime`/`Speed`, `Evaluate`, layers/AvatarMasks, root motion, IK, `AnimancerGraph`/`Playable` access). For each, count call sites and say what it's used for (gameplay presentation playback, Ability Lab timeline scrubbing like `PlayerRenderer.PlayScrubbed`, editor preview, cooking/pose sampling, tests). Call out anything that would be hard to reproduce with plain `PlayableGraph` + `AnimationClipPlayable` + `AnimationMixerPlayable` (e.g. events, complex mixers, transitions assets serialized in data).
3. **Serialized usage**: do any tracked `.prefab`, `.unity`, `.asset` files contain Animancer components or Animancer-typed serialized fields? Get the script GUIDs from the local package's `.cs.meta` files (e.g. AnimancerComponent, NamedAnimancerComponent, HybridAnimancerComponent, any transition asset types) and `git grep` the tracked YAML for those GUIDs. Also check `CharacterAssetCatalog` assets/scripts: do they store Animancer types (e.g. `ClipTransition`) or plain `AnimationClip` references?
4. **Is Animancer used outside presentation?** Specifically: does the character cook / deterministic pose sampling (search `sloparena.character.cook`, pose sampling, `SampleAnimation`, `AnimationMode`, `PoseTrack`, pose baking code under `client/Unity/Assets/Scripts/Editor/` and `client/Unity/Assets/AbilityLab/`) depend on Animancer, or on Unity's built-in `AnimationClip.SampleAnimation`/Playables? This matters a lot: if cooking needs Animancer, editing moves without it breaks.
5. Existing decisions: read `docs/systems/animation-system.md`, `docs/plans/2026-10-13-unity-dependency-ownership.md`, `docs/contributing/unity-setup.md` and any ADR mentioning Animancer (`git grep -n -i animancer -- docs`). Summarize what the docs already say about Animancer ownership, version (8.4.0?), Pro vs Lite, and any plan to make it optional or replace it.
6. Also check whether Animancer *Pro-only* features are used (fade durations other than default, `AnimancerState.Time` setting in builds, mixers, etc.), since Lite restricts some features in runtime builds.

Finish with: a short verdict on the size of the seam (number of files/call sites), the recommended route (optional-with-fallback vs replace-with-Playables vs keep-as-required) with the concrete reasons from the code, and the risky spots. Be precise; I will base an architecture recommendation on this.

input.description: Audit missing-asset runtime behavior
input.prompt:
Context: SLOPArena is a Unity 6 platform fighter (public GitHub repo). Gameplay is a deterministic C# simulation in `src/Shared/`; Unity presents it. A fresh clone lacks most art: 184 of 251 character asset dependencies are absent (docs/assets/contributor-inputs.md), stage prefabs `client/Unity/Assets/Resources/Stages/*.prefab` are gitignored, plus vendor VFX/audio/icons. The maintainer's new north star: **a fresh clone can run the game (at least Training) and the Slop Editor (Ability Lab) even without those assets**; gameplay/hitboxes should still work because they come from cooked deterministic data. They are also starting to remake assets/animations themselves so those will be distributable. I need to know what currently happens when assets are missing and what's already planned. Read-only; thoroughness: very thorough.

Use the clean checkout at `/home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena/.worktrees/friends-onboarding` (tracked files only, matches origin/main). Don't analyze Animancer itself (another agent is on that) and don't do a GUID-by-GUID scan of scenes (I'm doing that).

Report, with file paths and line numbers:

1. **What's already planned or decided.** Summarize `docs/plans/2026-10-13-public-reference-kit.md`, `docs/plans/2026-10-13-unity-dependency-ownership.md`, `docs/plans/2026-10-13-contributor-cleanup.md`, `docs/contributing/unity-setup.md`, `docs/assets/contributor-inputs.md`, `docs/adr/0031-character-asset-dependency-classification.md`, and `tools/check_unity_setup.py`. Which parts of "run without assets" are already decided, deferred, or explicitly rejected? Quote the key sentences.
2. **Cooked data vs Unity assets.** What exactly is in `content-cooked/<package>/` (list the files for one package and what each contains)? Does the cooked pose data contain per-tick bone/hurtbox transforms for every move, enough that (a) the Shared simulation needs no Unity asset at all, and (b) a fallback renderer could draw a "capsule mannequin" (hurtbox capsules posed from cooked data) with no rig? Identify the pose data format/types in `src/Shared/` and which bones/hurtboxes it covers.
3. **Character presentation when assets are missing.** Trace how the client builds a fighter's visuals: `PlayerRenderer` (or equivalent), how it resolves the rig/prefab/avatar/clips from `CharacterAssetCatalog` / generated client bindings. What happens if the rig prefab, avatar, or clips are null/missing — null checks, fallbacks, exceptions, or fail-closed admission (e.g. does the content admission refuse the package when presentation bindings don't resolve)? Is there any existing placeholder/fallback visual (capsule, debug mannequin, hurtbox gizmo renderer)?
4. **Stages when the prefab is missing.** `StageSelectController` skips stages whose `Resources/Stages/<name>.prefab` is missing — confirm, and check what Training and the offline arena scene do without a prefab. The baked collision in `data/arenas/*` is tracked: is there any existing code that renders collision geometry (debug or gray-box) that could serve as a fallback stage visual?
5. **Other presentation dependencies**: VFX (e.g. Cartoon FX prefabs), audio (`Resources/Audio/SFX`, `CombatSFX.cs`, `UISFX.cs`), UI icons (`Resources/Icons`), fonts, shaders/materials, post-processing. For each: null-safe or throws?
6. **Ability Lab / Slop Editor without assets.** What does it need to open and to preview a move: the cooked package, the rig, the clips? Is the hitbox/hurtbox overlay drawn from cooked Shared data or from live Animator bones? Can a user edit gameplay values (timings, hitbox sizes/positions, damage) and **Save + Cook** without the source clips/rig — or does the cook re-sample clips and fail? Find the cook code path and what it requires; note any "reuse existing pose data" or stale-input handling.
7. **Training/Frontend boot path**: anything in the boot path (Frontend scene → Training) that hard-requires an untracked asset (e.g. `Resources.Load` of a missing asset followed by a non-null assumption)? List the most likely first exceptions a clean clone would hit.

End with a prioritized list: the smallest set of code changes needed so a clean clone can (1) compile, (2) boot to Training and play with placeholder visuals, (3) open Ability Lab, scrub a move with hitbox overlays, and (4) edit + cook gameplay values. For each, say whether the change is small/medium/large and where it goes. Be precise and blunt; I'm basing an architecture recommendation on this.

- **Compiling:** Animancer is the only thing stopping a fresh clone from compiling. It's used in 6 files, 2 of them runtime code (`PlayerRenderer.cs` and `AbilityLab.cs`).

  # Animancer dependency audit
  
  **Bottom line:** Animancer is used only for presentation, and the dependency is shallow. Six tracked C# files use its types. Five of them are editor or test code, and every runtime gameplay use sits in `PlayerRenderer.cs`. That code uses a small part of Animancer: one default layer, one clip state per clip, crossfades, Time, Speed, `Evaluate` and `Stop`. It uses no events, mixers, layers, masks, transitions, IK or root motion. The character cook does not use Animancer. It uses `AnimationClip.SampleAnimation`. The one hidden link: the cook hashes `packages-lock.json`, and that file lists Animancer.
  
  **Recommendation:** replace Animancer with an in-house player built on the Playables API, and put it behind the `PlayerRenderer` API, which already acts as the seam. Reasons and risky spots are at the end.
  
  Audited on the clean worktree `/home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena/.worktrees/friends-onboarding` at `77c45b66`. I read the main checkout only for the Animancer package's `package.json`, asmdefs and `.meta` files.
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Tracked C# files that reference Animancer, by assembly
